title: Semantic model best practices (optimization + AI-readiness)
summary: How to optimize a Power BI semantic model for performance, correctness, and use as an AI/data-agent source: run the Best Practice Analyzer, fix descriptions/naming/aggregation/relationships, understand measure dependencies, and know which AI-prep steps are portal-only. Based on Microsoft's 'Semantic model best practices for data agent' guidance.
why_it_matters: A bloated or poorly-modeled semantic model produces slow, inaccurate results — especially when a Fabric data agent generates DAX against it. A clean star schema with descriptive names, correct default summarization, and good descriptions makes both reports and AI answers faster and more accurate.

fabio_commands.semantic-model analyze: Best Practice Analyzer / Memory Analyzer over the model's INFO.VIEW metadata. Flags missing descriptions, cryptic names, implicit-aggregation risks (identifier columns that still sum), duplicate/overlapping measures, ambiguous date fields, relationship hygiene (inactive/bidirectional/many-to-many), non-star (flat / no-relationship) schemas, and calculated columns. Add --with-cardinality to probe DISTINCTCOUNT and flag high-cardinality (memory-heavy) columns. Use --severity warning to focus, and --strict to fail CI on issues. Add --fix to auto-apply the ONE safe mechanical fix (set default summarization to None on identifier columns) via a dry-run-guarded definition overwrite — naming/dedup/schema/description issues are deliberately NOT auto-fixed (they can break DAX/relationships or need human judgment).
fabio_commands.semantic-model measure-dependencies: Lists each measure's dependencies (the measures/columns/tables its DAX references), read from the model definition. Use it to include ALL dependent objects when scoping an AI data schema — a measure that references other measures/columns needs those included too.
fabio_commands.semantic-model list-tables/list-columns/: INFO.VIEW.* introspection to understand the model (types, StorageMode, SummarizeBy, descriptions, cardinality of relationships) before optimizing or writing DAX.
fabio_commands.semantic-model generate: Generate a clean Direct Lake model from a lakehouse/warehouse (portal-exact TMDL). Start from a well-modeled source; generate does not create relationships/measures (add via update-definition). Prefer --storage-mode onelake (Direct Lake on OneLake, GA March 2026): OneLake security, more modeling features, faster queries, and multiple sources; use the default --storage-mode sql only when you depend on SQL-endpoint security rules or need DirectQuery fallback.
fabio_commands.semantic-model query: Validate the DAX the agent (or you) will run — response accuracy depends on the generated DAX being correct.
fabio_commands.data-agent evaluate: Evaluate a data agent's answers against ground-truth question/answer pairs (optionally with an LLM judge) to measure accuracy and iterate.
fabio_commands.data-agent update-config --enable-previe: Switch the data agent to the preview runtime to use Advanced DAX generation (multi-step reasoning + instance-value indexing) for its semantic-model sources — see advanced_dax_generation_preview below. Same toggle enables Advanced NL2SQL for SQL sources.
fabio_commands.git + deploy: Manage semantic model + data-agent configuration across dev/test/prod with Git integration and deployment pipelines (source control / ALM).

recommended_workflow: 1. Optimize the model: run `semantic-model analyze --with-cardinality` and fix the flagged issues (descriptions, naming, default summarization, high-cardinality columns, star schema).
2. Understand dependencies: `semantic-model measure-dependencies` so an AI data schema includes every dependent measure/column.
3. Add descriptions to tables/columns/measures (grounds the AI). fabio flags missing ones; author them in Power BI Desktop/Service or via update-definition.
4. Configure Prep for AI (AI data schema, verified answers, AI instructions) — see the note below; this is portal/Desktop-only today.
5. Add the model to the data agent and select the SAME tables you scoped in Prep for AI.
6. Test: run questions and verify the answers are correct (`data-agent query`; validate a question set with `data-agent evaluate`).
7. Evaluate & iterate with `data-agent evaluate` against ground-truth pairs.
8. Put it under source control and promote with deploy/deployment pipelines.
common_pitfalls: Flat/denormalized tables instead of a star schema — analyze flags 'flat-schema'/'no-relationships'.
Implicit measures / wrong default summarization on numeric identifier columns — analyze flags 'implicit-aggregation'. Set SummarizeBy=None on keys and create explicit measures.
Duplicate/overlapping measures (Total Sales / Sales Amount / Revenue) create ambiguity — analyze flags 'duplicate-measure'.
Cryptic names (TR_AMT, DIM_GEO_01) — analyze flags 'non-descriptive-name'. Use business-friendly names or descriptions/synonyms.
Ambiguous date fields (Order Date, Ship Date, ...) without guidance — analyze flags 'ambiguous-dates'. Mark a date table and add AI instructions.
Verified answers referencing hidden fields won't work.
Including helper/intermediate measures in the AI data schema adds noise — include only real business metrics (use measure-dependencies to know what's required).

advanced_dax_generation_preview.what: 'Advanced DAX generation' is the semantic-model counterpart of Advanced NL2SQL — the multi-step-reasoning DAX tool a data agent uses on its PREVIEW RUNTIME. Unlike standard DAX generation (single pass), it inspects model metadata, interprets the question, resolves ambiguity, and refines the DAX across multiple reasoning steps.
advanced_dax_generation_preview.enable_with_fabio: It is the SAME toggle as Advanced NL2SQL: `fabio data-agent update-config --workspace <ws> --id <agent> --enable-preview-runtime` (on the wire: experimental.enableExperimentalFeatures). `--disable-preview-runtime` reverts to standard single-pass DAX generation. Verify with `data-agent get-config` (its previewRuntime field). A published agent's runtime is fixed at publish time — republish to change it.
advantages: More accurate answers to complex questions (iterative reasoning + result inspection).
Instance value indexing — searches actual column values to build reliable filters.
Consistency across Fabric data agent, Fabric skills, Power BI, M365 Copilot, and Fabric IQ.
Lower latency in some scenarios (more efficient object/value identification).
advanced_dax_generation_preview.instance_value_indexing_requirement: Instance value indexing currently requires the semantic model's Q&A setting to be enabled (on by default for Import and Direct Lake models). Q&A retires in December 2026; a replacement setting will support it afterward.
advanced_dax_generation_preview.note: Advanced DAX generation uses the same semantic-model metadata + Prep for AI configuration described below — enabling the preview runtime does NOT replace good modeling and Prep for AI; it amplifies it.

portal_only_note: The three 'Prep for AI' components — AI data schema, verified answers, and AI instructions — are configured in Power BI Desktop or the Power BI service ('Prep data for AI'), NOT via a public Fabric/Power BI REST API, so fabio cannot set them today. IMPORTANT: the DAX-generation tool (standard AND the preview Advanced DAX generation) ONLY uses the semantic model's metadata + Prep for AI config; it IGNORES data-agent-level instructions for semantic-model DAX. Keep model-specific guidance in Prep for AI; use data-agent instructions only for cross-source concerns (formatting, routing, tone). fabio helps with everything else: model health (analyze), dependencies (measure-dependencies), descriptions (flagging), preview-runtime toggle (data-agent update-config --enable-preview-runtime), evaluation (data-agent evaluate), and ALM (git/deploy).
